questions.question: Oxidation is defined as:
The oxidising agent in a redox reaction is the substance that:
options: Causes oxidation in the other substance by taking its electrons, and is itself reduced
Donates electrons to the other substance

questions.question: When zinc metal reacts with copper ions, zinc is the:
options: Oxidising agent, because it is reduced
Reducing agent, because it donates electrons and is itself oxidised

questions.question: In any electrochemical cell, the anode is the electrode where:
A galvanic cell converts:
options: Chemical energy to electrical energy via a spontaneous redox reaction

questions.question: In the zinc-copper cell, electrons flow through the external wire:
As the zinc-copper cell operates, the observations include:
options: Zinc electrode loses mass, copper electrode gains mass, the blue colour fades
The copper dissolves and the solution turns bluer

questions.question: The functions of the salt bridge are to:
options: Complete the circuit and maintain electrical neutrality in both half-cells

questions.question: Standard conditions for electrode potentials are:
options: Concentration 1 mol·dm⁻³, temperature 25 °C, gases at standard pressure

questions.question: The reference electrode assigned a potential of exactly 0 V is the:
The more positive a half-reaction's electrode potential, the stronger the substance on its left is as:
options: An oxidising agent — it grabs electrons more fiercely

questions.question: When two half-cells are paired in a galvanic cell, the half-cell with the higher electrode potential becomes:
In standard cell notation, the double vertical line represents:
Cell notation is written with:
options: The cathode on the left and anode on the right
The anode on the left and the cathode on the right

questions.question: For the zinc-copper cell (E° values −0,76 V and +0,34 V), the emf E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode is:
A 'flat' galvanic cell delivers no emf because:
options: The salt bridge is used up
The cell reaction has reached equilibrium — no net tendency to push electrons remains

questions.question: Dropping zinc directly into copper sulfate solution wastes the reaction's energy as:
options: Heat, because the electron transfer happens on the spot

questions.question: A galvanic cell harvests the same reaction as electricity by:
options: Adding a catalyst to the beaker
Separating giver and taker so the electrons must travel through the external wire

questions.question: In the transaction picture, a flat battery is best described as:
options: A finished transaction — the chemistry has reached its resting point

subtopics.title: The Bridge That Keeps the Peace

questions.question: Without a salt bridge, the anode beaker would quickly:
options: Build up positive charge, halting the electron flow

questions.question: The salt bridge maintains neutrality by:
options: Releasing negative ions toward the anode beaker and positive ions toward the cathode beaker
Absorbing the extra zinc ions into the glass

questions.question: In the two-storey picture of the circuit, current is carried by:
options: Electrons in the wire and ions in the solutions and bridge

questions.question: Pulling the salt bridge out of a working cell causes the voltmeter to:

subtopics.title: The League Table of Electron Grabbers

questions.question: In the league-table picture, the substances with large positive electrode potentials are:
options: The fiercest electron grabbers — strongest oxidising agents

questions.question: When any two substances are paired, the spontaneous direction is decided by:
options: The stronger grabber taking electrons from the weaker one

questions.question: Pairing magnesium (−2,36 V) with silver (+0,80 V) gives a cell emf of:
Choosing two half-reactions that sit close together on the table produces a cell with:
options: A small emf — a small gap means a small push per electron
